issue.title: Proc-store read counters in test_monitor_store_reconcile.py are process-global, so background reconciliation from other tests inflates them under the full parallel lane
issue.description:
DISCOVERED BY: agent 044 as a DISCOVERED ISSUE note on closed epic sase-n7 ('Get monitor reconciliation off the ACE startup critical path'), 2026-08-16T18:16:52Z, observed on master 57c71d17a. Root cause diagnosed during the sase-n7 landing.

FAILING NODES (both added by sase-n7.5, commit 0ec2018f1's sibling work in phase n7.2/n7.3):
  tests/monitor/test_monitor_store_reconcile.py::test_reconcile_dead_supervisors_reads_proc_store_once
  tests/monitor/test_monitor_store_reconcile.py::test_list_monitors_proc_store_reads_do_not_scale_with_record_count

REPRODUCTION: During finish_m9_proc_closeout verification, 'just check' escalated to the full 14-worker lane and failed both. Both pass immediately together in isolation, and the focused monitor/proc lane passed 221/221. That pass-in-isolation / fail-in-full-lane shape is cross-module contamination, not a logic error.

ROOT CAUSE: Both assertions count proc-store reads through a PROCESS-GLOBAL monkeypatch with no thread or task scoping.
  - _count_proc_store_reads (tests/monitor/test_monitor_store_reconcile.py:641) replaces sase.procs.store._call_binding with a closure that appends every 'read_procs_snapshot' call to a plain list, then asserts 'reads == ["read_procs_snapshot"]' (exactly one).
  - test_list_monitors_proc_store_reads_do_not_scale_with_record_count builds its own equivalent 'counting' closure inline (same file, ~line 532) and asserts '1 <= small <= 2' and 'small == large'.
Any caller anywhere in the process that touches read_procs_snapshot while the patch is installed lands in that counter.

WHY IT ONLY STARTED NOW: sase-n7.4 (39bdd6772) moved _reconcile_dead_monitor_supervisors_for_tui (src/sase/ace/tui/actions/agents/_loading_disk_support.py:108) off the synchronous agents disk load and onto a background asyncio task via spawn_pump_free_task (src/sase/ace/tui/util/pump_tasks.py:64). Before that change, reconciliation only ran inline on the load path and could not overlap an unrelated test. Now any concurrently-running ACE TUI test in the same xdist worker can emit a read_procs_snapshot that the monitor tests' counters attribute to themselves. The counters were written in the same epic, under the pre-existing assumption that no concurrent caller exists.

SCOPE / LIKELY FIX: scope the counting to the call under test rather than to the process — record the owning thread ident (and/or asyncio task) when the patch is installed and only count reads originating from it, or have reconcile/list_monitors surface their own read count so the assertion does not depend on a global patch. Applies to both the shared helper and the inline closure. Verify under the full parallel lane, not just the focused monitor lane, since the focused lane already passes.

NOT ATTEMPTED HERE: the sase-n7 land agent diagnosed but did not fix this, because a speculative change to a regression gate could not be verified under the 14-worker conditions that produce the failure within that agent's turn.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-n7 — closed epic that caused this. Phase sase-n7.4 (39bdd6772) created the background reconciliation caller and phase sase-n7.2/n7.3 wrote the process-global counters that assume no concurrent caller. Its land agent recorded this diagnosis but did not fix it.
